summary: A thief can teleport the car they are driving (and therefore network-own) into their own drop-off, and the delivery is accepted before the anti-cheat watchdog ever checks the move. This makes an instant, permanent theft of another player's car possible (also an instant Loot delivery or Chop Shop payout).
evidence: VehicleService.luau:1728-1757: the zone pass runs every 0.2s (ZONE_TICK) and the watchdog every 0.5s (WATCHDOG_TICK). When both are due in the same Heartbeat, runPass("zone") (1739-1742) runs before runPass("watchdog") (1743-1746). zonePass (1460-1498) reads the client-replicated `car.chassis.CFrame.Position` and calls fireDelivery (1478-1483) or ChopAttempt (1489-1491) with no plausibility check. The watchdog verdict (_watchdogVerdict, 395-406) only rewinds the car in violate() (1500-1542); it never blocks or undoes zone events. Downstream nothing re-checks travel either: GarageService.onDelivery calls Theft.complete (1075), or storeCar for Loot (1100); TheftService.complete (1223-1384) only checks theft/driver/free slots and never looks at theft.startedAt against the distance travelled; onChop pays chopValue (1159-1163).
failureScenario: An exploiter holds the StealPrompt on a victim's display car. beginTheft seats them, and VehicleService.seat gives them network ownership (947). Their client then calls `car.model:PivotTo(<own DropOffCFrame>)`. Within 0.2s zonePass fires DeliveryAttempt and TheftService.complete runs removeSlot(victim) and storeCar(thief), then saveNow on both profiles. The victim's car is gone for good in under a second, with no chase and no counterplay. The watchdog fires afterwards on a car that is already destroyed. The same trick delivers any street, dealer or Hot Drop Loot car instantly, skips the police, and farms Chop Shop cash by teleporting Loot cars into the chop zone.
suggestedFix:
Make zone triggers depend on a trusted position:
(1) In zonePass, before firing DeliveryAttempt/ChopAttempt/SprayAttempt, run the watchdog check for that car against st.wdCFrame/st.wdAt. Skip zones if the verdict is not nil or `now < st.wdRevokedUntil`. Simplest version: run watchdogPass at ZONE_TICK and order it before zonePass.
(2) Require that the previous accepted sample was within `cap*dt + slack` of the drop-off box.
(3) In TheftService.complete, reject when `hooks.clock() - theft.startedAt < (slotWorld(victimPlot,slot) - dropoff(thiefPlot)).Magnitude / VehicleService.getSpeedCap(car)`. Apply the same minimum-time rule to Loot cars using their spawn position and time (store car.data.spawnPos / spawnedAt), and to chop.
(4) Record watchdog violations per car (e.g. car.data.tainted = true) and refuse delivery or chop for tainted cars.
verifyReason: Confirmed. VehicleService.seat (947) and setDriver (839) give the driver network ownership. zonePass (1460-1498) reads the client-replicated chassis.CFrame and fires DeliveryAttempt/ChopAttempt with no plausibility check. The zone pass runs every 0.2s and is ordered before the 0.5s watchdog in Heartbeat (1739-1746), so a teleport into the drop-off is delivered within 0.2s, before any watchdog sample. violate() only rewinds the car. Nothing downstream checks travel: GarageService.onDelivery -> Theft.complete (1075), storeCar for Loot (1100), onChop (1146-1163). TheftService.complete checks only the theft, driver, free slots and the victim record; it never uses theft.startedAt or distance. Any executor can permanently take other players' cars (victim online, >=3 cars, not on cooldown), deliver Loot or Hot Drop cars instantly, or farm Chop cash by teleporting street cars. Reordering the passes alone is not enough. When a car stands still, watchdogPass keeps wdCFrame and lets the allowance grow for up to WATCHDOG_MAX_DT=3s. That allows a legal jump of cap*3+10, where cap is about 2.1x topSpeed, so roughly 500-900 studs. The nearest plots are 480 studs apart (Map.Plots on a 160-stud grid). A thief could freeze for 3s and then jump into a neighbour's drop-off without a verdict. A minimum-travel-time gate is needed as well.
fix:
1) src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau: move the per-car body of watchdogPass (1547-1580) into a local checkCar(player, car, st, now): string? and call it at the top of zonePass's loop, before _zoneFlags. If it returns a verdict (violate() already rewinds) or now < st.wdRevokedUntil, `continue` without touching st.inDropoff/inChop/inSpray. Keep watchdogPass for non-zone ticks.
2) Add a time gate the 3s freeze allowance cannot get around. In setDriver(car, player), when a drive begins (car.data.driveStartAt == nil, or the driver changed), record car.data.driveStartAt = os.clock() and car.data.driveStartPos = chassis.Position. Expose VehicleService.minTravelTime(car, targetPos) = flat(targetPos - car.data.driveStartPos).Magnitude / (car.def.topSpeed * SPEED_CAP_MULT * NITRO_SPEED_MULT) (no lag grace).
3) src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau complete(): before the point of no return, return false (the theft stays active) if hooks.clock() - theft.startedAt < (MapLayout.slotWorld(victimPlot, theft.slot).Position - MapLayout.plotDropoffZone(thiefPlot).Position).Magnitude / maxSpeed(car).
4) src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau onDelivery (Loot branch) and onChop: return early if os.clock() - car.data.driveStartAt < VehicleService.minTravelTime(car, pos).
5) In violate(), set car.data.tainted = true. Have onDelivery/onChop/Theft.complete refuse tainted cars; for a Stolen car, fail the theft so it returns home.

summary: An Owned car left in the world when its owner leaves can be driven home after the owner rejoins the same server. If that slot's record is gone by then, GarageService stores the car again, which duplicates it.
evidence: GarageService.onDelivery (1031-1053): if `rec and rec.carId == car.carId` it restores the slot; otherwise it calls `GarageService.storeCar(player, car.carId, car.mutation)` (1046-1052), with the comment "the slot vanished meanwhile (rebirth...): try to keep the car anyway". On leave, GarageService.cleanup (1226-1235) clears pstates and displays but never destroys ps.outCars. VehicleService.onPlayerRemoving (1684-1696) only calls setDriver(car, nil). The orphan Owned car therefore lives about OWNED_RETURN_AFTER = 20s (Config/Vehicle.luau:72; lifePass 1647-1651). onEnterTriggered (1160-1167) lets any player whose UserId equals car.ownerUserId get in, and that includes a new Player object for the same account. In the new session the slot state map is fresh, so sellSlot (855) and RebirthService.blockedReason (173-189) both treat the slot as Parked.
failureScenario:
1. The player drives car X out of slot 3 (state Driving), parks outside the garage and leaves. The release save stores slot 3 = X.
2. They rejoin the same server (private server or follow-a-friend) within about 20s. The profile loads with X on display in slot 3.
3. They sell slot 3 via the SellCar remote, or rebirth.
4. They walk to the orphan X (the EnterPrompt allows them) and drive it into their drop-off. leftGarage is already true. onDelivery finds rec == nil and calls storeCar, so X is back in the garage and the sale cash or rebirth is kept. This repeats every cycle.
suggestedFix:
(1) In onDelivery and onReturnedHome, never call storeCar for an Owned car. If `rec == nil or rec.carId ~= car.carId`, destroy the car and log it.
(2) On PlayerRemoving, destroy every Owned car for that player: iterate ps.outCars in GarageService.cleanup before clearing pstates, and/or in VehicleService.onPlayerRemoving destroy cars with `kind == "Owned" and ownerUserId == player.UserId`.
(3) Stamp Owned cars with the DataService session id (or the Player instance) at spawn and require a match in onEnterTriggered and onDelivery.
verifyReason: Confirmed, with a timeline easier than the one reported. GarageService.cleanup (1226-1235) and VehicleService.onPlayerRemoving (1684-1696) never destroy the leaver's Owned car, so it survives OWNED_RETURN_AFTER=20s (lifePass 1647-1650). The release write and the same-server reclaim take about 7-15s: lockState treats a dead local session as stale, and the claim waits keyWriteCooldown 6.2s. The new pstate has empty states/outCars, so getSlotState returns "Parked" for the slot whose car is still out. onEnterTriggered (1160-1167) authorises by UserId, so the new Player object can get in. The player only has to get into the orphan car within 20s; after that nothing is timed. They can then fire SellCar(slot) (no proximity check) while driving and enter their drop-off. leftGarage is already true. onDelivery finds rec nil (or a different carId if the slot was refilled) and calls storeCar (1046-1052). Result: they keep the car plus 50% of its price, or keep it across a rebirth. This is an infinite-cash dupe, repeatable with a private server or a client TeleportToPlaceInstance to the same JobId.
fix:
1) src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau onDelivery, Owned branch: require session ownership and an intact record. `local ps = getPS(player); if not (slot and ps.outCars[slot] == car and rec and rec.carId == car.carId) then car.data.delivered = true; destroyCar(car, "orphan"); return end`. Delete the storeCar fallback (1046-1052) entirely; an Owned car must never create a new record.
2) Defence in depth in src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau onPlayerRemoving: after setDriver(car, nil), loop `for _, c in VehicleService.all() do if c.kind == "Owned" and c.ownerUserId == player.UserId then VehicleService.destroy(c, "owner_left") end end`. This is safe because GarageService.getSlotState returns nil or "Parked" for an unloaded or cleared player, so onVehicleDestroyed does nothing.

summary: The server's hold-time check on garage and dealership steal prompts only records when a hold began. It never clears that time when the hold ends and has no upper bound, so a short tap made earlier satisfies the check at any later time.
evidence: GarageService.luau:552-563: PromptButtonHoldBegan stores `display.holds[p] = os.clock()`; Triggered accepts if `os.clock() - began >= _requiredHold(...)`; there is no PromptButtonHoldEnded handler. DealershipService.luau:836-839 + 723-733 (steal) and 813-821 + 652-660 (buy) use the same pattern, and their holds are cleared only by clearPad or PlayerRemoving. The EventService fallback hot-drop prompt (812-836) has the same issue and also no server distance check. Compare VehicleService.addStealPrompt 1061-1067, which clears an interrupted hold. Even that version keeps a completed hold indefinitely, with no maximum age.
failureScenario: An exploiter taps a victim's display car StealPrompt for 0.1s; the server records `began`. They release, set `prompt.HoldDuration = 0` locally (client-only), wait out of sight or until the victim's laser lock expires, then press again. The client fires Triggered immediately, with no new HoldBegan, and the stale `began` passes. The steal (or dealer Mythic steal) is effectively instant, with no visible hold for the victim to respond to. This also cheapens the Hotwire upgrade and the Master Thief gamepass.
suggestedFix:
Use one shared validated-hold helper (as in VehicleService) for every hold prompt:
- On PromptButtonHoldEnded, clear holds[p] when `now - began < required*tol`.
- In Triggered, reject when `now - began > required + 1.5` (stale arm).
- Clear holds on PlayerRemoving.
For GarageService, call VehicleService.addStealPrompt-style logic, or port those handlers. Add a withinReach check to the EventService fallback prompt.
verifyReason: Confirmed for GarageService (552-563): holds[p] is set on HoldBegan, there is no HoldEnded handler, and there is no upper bound on age. The same holds for DealershipService steal (723-733, 836-839). An exploit client that taps once and later fires Triggered with a local HoldDuration of 0 (no new HoldBegan) passes the check. For player garages this removes the whole defence window, up to 6*1.4=8.4s for Mythic/Secret, in which owners can bonk the thief. It also devalues the Hotwire upgrade and the Master Thief pass. Distance is still checked later in TheftService.beginTheft and in Dealership nearPad, so the exploit needs presence at the car and only saves the hold. The dealer buy pre-arm is harmless. The EventService fallback prompt (812-836) is effectively dead code: it runs only if VehicleService.addStealPrompt is missing or throws. VehicleService.addStealPrompt does clear interrupted holds but has no max age.
fix: src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau (display StealPrompt): add `steal.PromptButtonHoldEnded:Connect(function(p) local b = display.holds[p]; if b and os.clock() - b < GarageService._requiredHold(base, holdMultiplier(p)) then display.holds[p] = nil end end)`. In Triggered, reject when `os.clock() - began > req / 0.9 + 1.5` (stale arm). Apply the same two changes to DealershipService steal (pad.stealHolds; onSteal) and add the max-age check to VehicleService.addStealPrompt's Triggered. Clear display.holds[p] and pad.stealHolds[p] on PlayerRemoving (GarageService holds are strong-keyed). The EventService fallback can be left alone, or given withinReach plus the same checks.

summary: The recovery and revenge bonuses have no minimum theft duration or distance and no per-thief/victim pair limit. Two colluding accounts can stage endless fake thefts to mint cash.
evidence: TheftService.onDriverChanged (1495-1496) calls markDropped as soon as the thief leaves the seat. The victim's RecoverPrompt (758-773) needs only a 0.15s hold, and recover() pays `_bonus(income, RECOVERY_BONUS_SECONDS=30)` with a $100 minimum (1425-1426). onThiefHit pays revenge once per theft when the victim bonks the thief (1466-1472, REVENGE_BONUS_SECONDS=20). The only throttle is THEFT_VICTIM_COOLDOWN = 25s (Economy.luau:133). beginTheft also grants the thief `steal` contract progress (1199).
failureScenario: A main account (3 or more cars) and an alt are on the same server. The alt holds Steal on main's car, gets seated, and hops out right away. Main bonks the alt (revenge: 20s of income) and presses Recover (30s of income). The car goes home and the cycle repeats every ~30s. That is about 50s of income per 30s, on top of normal income. The alt also farms steal5/steal12 contracts and main farms `defend`.
suggestedFix: Pay the recovery and revenge bonuses only when the theft lasted at least N seconds and the car got at least M studs from the victim's slot (track the max distance in _tick). Add a per-(victimUserId, thiefUserId) bonus cooldown, e.g. one bonus per pair per 10 minutes. Award `steal` progress for player thefts only on complete().
verifyReason: Confirmed and needs no exploit tools; two friends can do it. beginTheft sets only the 25s victim cooldown. onDriverChanged -> markDropped as soon as the thief hops out. The RecoverPrompt needs a 0.15s server-side hold (RECOVER_HOLD 0.3*0.5) and recover() pays _bonus(income, 30s) (min $100) whenever restoreVictimSlot succeeds. onThiefHit pays 20s of income once per theft when the victim bonks the thief. Nothing checks how long the theft lasted, how far the car travelled, or how often the same pair repeats. Repeating every ~25s pays the victim about 50s of income per 25s (+~200% income). The thief also gets `steal` contract progress at begin (1199). Contracts are capped at 3 per day, so that part is minor.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau: in _tick, track theft.leftPlot = true once MapLayout.plotAt(carPosition(car)) ~= plotIndexOf(victim). In recover() and in the in-theft revenge branch of onThiefHit, pay the bonus only if theft.leftPlot and hooks.clock() - theft.startedAt >= ~10s. Add a module-level bonusPairs[victimUserId..":"..thiefUserId] timestamp and skip both bonuses if the pair was paid within the last 600s. Optionally move progress(thief, "steal", 1) from beginTheft to complete().

summary: A completed theft moves a car between two separate DataStore keys using two parallel, unordered saves. A crash or rejected write between them can leave the car in both profiles.
evidence:
TheftService.complete 1329-1336 spawns `DS.saveNow(thief)` and `DS.saveNow(victim)` at the same time. Each one waits on its own per-key cooldown (DataService.waitForKeyCooldown 602-610, up to 6.2s). The thief's write can land while the victim's is still queued. If the victim's write is then lost (hard crash, or session-lost outcome in writeAsync 763-766 after a forced lock steal in claimAsync 635/652), the DataStore holds the car under both keys.

DataService is otherwise sound:
- session-locked UpdateAsync loads and saves
- failed loads kick instead of loading defaults
- BindToClose flush
- schema version + migration hook
- receipt ids stored in the same record as the grant
- capped receipts and retired-car arrays
AdminService gating (IsStudio / creator / group rank 255, checked on every call) is also correct, and every Net.on/Net.handle argument is type- and range-checked.
failureScenario: The victim had a write about 2s earlier (autosave, or a dealership purchase of $50k or more that calls saveNow). A theft completes; the thief's save lands at once and the victim's waits about 4s. The server crashes in that window, so BindToClose never runs. On rejoin both players own the car.
suggestedFix: Order the transfer so a failure loses the car rather than duplicating it: `task.spawn(function() if DS.saveNow(victim) then DS.saveNow(thief) end end)`. Alternatively record a transfer id in the thief's profile (pendingTransfers) and reconcile on the victim's next load. At minimum, never persist the thief's addition before the victim's removal is durable.
verifyReason: Confirmed but narrow. complete() spawns saveNow(thief) and saveNow(victim) in parallel (1329-1336), and each waits on its own 6.2s key cooldown, so the thief's write can land first. Duplication needs a hard crash with no BindToClose, or a lost victim session, inside that window. Reordering saveNow only partly helps: the independent autosaveLoop can also persist the thief before the victim. Only a transfer log is truly atomic, and that is out of proportion for an 8-player game. The DataService strengths listed in the finding are accurate.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau complete(): replace the two spawns with one sequential task, `hooks.spawnTask(function() pcall(DS.saveNow, victim); pcall(DS.saveNow, thief) end)`, so the explicit saves remove before they add. Accept the remaining autosave-ordering risk, or later record a transfer id (pendingTransfers) on the thief and reconcile it on the victim's load.

summary: The code checks whether seating the thief worked by looking at the `call()` helper's first return value, but that value is pcall's success flag, not VehicleService.seat's result. A failed seat is never detected and the rollback code never runs.
evidence: In TheftService.luau, `call` (160-172) returns `true, res`. beginTheft does `local seatOk = call("VehicleService", "seat", car, thief); if not seatOk then failTheft(...)` (1190-1196), so seatOk is true even when seat returns `false, "not allowed"`. DealershipService.luau has the same pattern: 118-130 and 773-776.
failureScenario: If seat fails (character mid-respawn, already sitting), the player theft continues unseated. _tick then marks it dropped, and the victim can Recover it for a bonus, which feeds ECON-1. For a dealer steal, an unclaimed Loot car with ownerUserId nil sits on the pad; any bystander can EnterPrompt into it while the thief carries the wanted stars.
suggestedFix: Use the real result: `local okCall, seated = call("VehicleService", "seat", car, thief); if not (okCall and seated == true) then failTheft(theft, "error") ... end`. For the dealer, destroy the spawned car, restore the pad, and skip addHeat when seating fails.
verifyReason: Confirmed. TheftService.call (160-172) and DealershipService.call (118-130) return pcall's success flag first. VehicleService.seat returns (false, reason) without throwing, so `local seatOk = call(...)` is true even when seating fails. The rollback in beginTheft (1190-1196) never runs. In practice seat rarely fails right after a validated prompt trigger: the thief is alive and nearby, and seat ejects them from any other car. The result then depends on the case. A player theft falls through to the _tick grace -> markDropped -> abandon path; the victim can Recover it, but ECON-1 does not need this bug. For a dealer steal, the Loot car is spawned without ownerUserId, so any bystander can EnterPrompt it while the thief keeps the heat. The same pattern exists in GarageService.driveSlot (pcall(VS.seat)), where it is harmless.
fix: TheftService.beginTheft: `local okCall, seated = call("VehicleService", "seat", car, thief); if not (okCall and seated == true) then failTheft(theft, "error"); notify(...); return false end`. DealershipService.onSteal: same check. On failure, call VS.destroy(car, "error"), restore the pad (undo clearPad / restock), skip addHeat and progress, and notify the player. Alternatively pass ownerUserId = player.UserId in the spawn opts so a failed seat at least stays claimable only by the thief.

summary: The bat's "in front of you" check accepts the client's aim point as an extra forward direction and does no line-of-sight raycast. Range is measured from the attacker's character position, which the client controls.
evidence: doBat (901-927) adds `aim - origin` to `forwards` whenever its magnitude is between 0.5 and 500. selectTarget (96-133) accepts a candidate in front of ANY forward. There is no Workspace:Raycast between attacker and victim for the bat, unlike doZap (980-997). applyHit (859-895) stuns, ejects from vehicles and triggers TheftService.onThiefHit revenge payouts.
failureScenario: An exploiter sends ToolAction("bat", victimRoot.Position) for whoever is within BAT_RANGE+2 in any direction, including through a garage wall. Combined with character teleporting, they can bonk-eject any driver: knock a thief out of a stolen car, or grief players at will.
suggestedFix: Ignore `aim` for the bat (use root.CFrame.LookVector only), or require `aimDir:Dot(lookVector) > 0.5`. Raycast from the attacker's head to the victim's root, excluding characters, and reject if world geometry blocks it. Optionally keep server-sampled root positions and reject hits right after implausible movement.
verifyReason: Partly confirmed. doBat (901-927) has no line-of-sight raycast, unlike doZap, so a bonk can pass through a 2-stud garage wall within BAT_RANGE+2=11 studs. The aim-as-forward complaint has no real effect: the attacker's root CFrame and LookVector are already client-owned, so an exploiter can just face the victim, and range from a client-controlled position is the generic character-teleport problem every Roblox melee has. Real impact is small: through-wall bonks at close range, and teleport-bonking drivers that a stronger cone would not stop either.
fix: src/server/Systems/CombatService.luau doBat: after selectTarget, raycast from the attacker's Head (or root + 1.5Y) to victimRoot.Position, with RaycastParams excluding both characters, the effects folder and the attacker's and victim's car models (reuse getZapParams). Reject if the ray hits anything else. Optionally drop the `aim` forward and use only root.CFrame.LookVector. It is mostly cosmetic either way.

summary: Playtime gifts reset every session, so rejoining re-grants them, including a Legendary car at 60 minutes. Referral car rewards to the inviter can be farmed with alt accounts.
evidence: PState.sessionStart and playtimeClaimed are runtime-only (RewardsService 241-280; claimPlaytime 552-571). Economy.PLAYTIME_REWARDS (150-157) includes `car` Rare at 15 min, Epic at 40 min and Legendary at 60 min. handleReferral (710-742) gives the inviter a REFERRAL_REWARD_RARITY (Epic) car for every new invitee account, with no cap per inviter.
failureScenario: An idle player with an auto-rejoin script gets a Rare, Epic and Legendary car every hour, instead of once per long session. An inviter brings fresh alts via referral links and gets one Epic car per alt.
suggestedFix: Persist playtime progress per UTC day (e.g. data.playtime = {day, seconds, claimed}) so rejoining does not reset it. Cap inviter referral rewards per day (store count/day in the inviter's data) and require the invitee to reach a minimum playtime before the inviter is paid.
verifyReason: Confirmed but mostly by design. SPEC/Economy comment: "minutes of play in the session -> reward". sessionStart and playtimeClaimed are runtime-only, so rejoining does not speed anything up; it only lets an AFK or anti-idle player repeat the 60-minute ladder (Rare, Epic, Legendary car) once per session-hour. handleReferral pays the inviter an Epic car per referred account with no per-inviter cap. The invitee flag (referralRewarded) is per account, so each alt pays out once. Farming needs alt accounts joining through the inviter's share link while the inviter is in the server.
fix: Product decision. For src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau, either persist playtime per UTC day (data.playtime = {day, seconds, claimed}, adding session seconds on Releasing) or drop the Legendary tier from the per-session ladder. For referrals, store data.referralsPaid = {day, count} on the inviter, cap it at ~3 per day, and pay the inviter only after the invitee has played about 10 minutes.

summary: The SellCar, BuyUpgrade and BuyTool remotes skip the proximity and hold requirements of the prompts they mirror.
evidence: The SellCar remote (GarageService 1296-1301 → sellSlot 848-881) has no distance check and no hold, while the in-world SellPrompt is a 1s hold at the display (532-546). The BuyUpgrade/BuyTool handlers (ShopService 249-260) do not require being near the Gear Shop counter, the only intended way to open the shop (OpenUI from the prompt at 204-210). Prices are correctly derived on the server.
failureScenario: A victim watches a thief start the 1.4×hotwireTime hold on their Mythic. From across the map they fire SellCar(slot) to cash out the instant before Triggered, denying the steal without being present. Players can also buy upgrades mid-chase from anywhere. The impact is gameplay fairness, not currency minting.
suggestedFix: If the in-world interaction is intended: SellCar should require the owner to be inside their plot (MapLayout.plotAt(root) == index), and Buy* should require the root within ~25 studs of a GearShopCounter part. Alternatively, accept remote use as a deliberate design choice.
verifyReason: Confirmed. The SellCar remote (GarageService 1296-1301 -> sellSlot 848-881) has no proximity check, while driveSlot does (DRIVE_MAX_DISTANCE / plotAt). No client code ever fires SellCar; only the in-world SellPrompt sells, so the remote is unused attack surface. Impact is limited to fairness, e.g. a victim cashing out at 50% during a thief's hold, and the victim loses the car either way. BuyUpgrade/BuyTool without proximity matches SPEC §202, which defines those remotes with only id/level/price validation. Treat that part as by design.
fix: src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau: in sellSlot (or the SellCar Net.on handler), require the same presence check driveSlot uses. Get the root; reject unless MapLayout.plotAt(root.Position) == plotIndexOf(player) or it is within DRIVE_MAX_DISTANCE of MapLayout.slotWorld(index, slot). Or remove the unused SellCar handler. Leave ShopService as is.

summary: The table of redeemable codes and their rewards lives in a container that is replicated to every client.
evidence: Economy.Codes (Economy.luau:196-201) is in ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Config, and RewardsService.redeemCode reads it on the server (579). Every client can require the module and read every code.
failureScenario: Unreleased or time-gated codes (e.g. QUACK = $5000) are datamined on release day and redeemed by everyone before the intended announcement.
suggestedFix: Move Codes into a server-only module (ServerScriptService/ServerStorage, e.g. src/server/Config/Codes.luau). Keep only non-secret display data in Shared.
verifyReason: Confirmed exposure, negligible impact. Economy.Codes lives in ReplicatedStorage and only RewardsService reads it (579). All four codes are live at launch, there is no time-gating or expiry field, and promo codes are meant to be public. It only matters if unannounced codes are staged in this table.
fix: Move the table to a server-only module (e.g. src/server/Config/Codes.luau, mapped under ServerScriptService) and require it from RewardsService.redeemCode. Remove Economy.Codes from Shared. No client code references it.

summary: The vehicle watchdog only checks horizontal speed and displacement. A client that owns a car can apply extreme spin or vertical velocity to fling other players and cars without triggering it.
evidence: watchdogPass (1544-1582) uses `flat(cf.Position - wdCFrame.Position)` and `flat(AssemblyLinearVelocity)`. AssemblyAngularVelocity and vertical motion are never checked or clamped while the driver owns the chassis (setDriver 839, seat 947).
failureScenario: An exploiter in any Loot car sets a huge AssemblyAngularVelocity and rams a thief's Stolen car or a victim's Owned car off the island. The theft fails with reason "lost" (TheftService 1543-1546), or the car is ejected and returned. Characters near the spawn plaza get flung repeatedly.
suggestedFix: In watchdogPass, also treat as a violation `chassis.AssemblyAngularVelocity.Magnitude > MAX_ANG` (e.g. 15 rad/s) and vertical speed above a cap. On violation, zero both velocities as violate() already does for linear velocity.
verifyReason: Confirmed. watchdogPass (1544-1582) measures only flat displacement and flat linear velocity, so a driver who owns the chassis can set a huge AssemblyAngularVelocity or vertical velocity undetected. Spinning a client-owned assembly is the classic fling. Fixing it for cars does not close the class, because the exploiter's own character (HumanoidRootPart) can fling the same way, but it does remove the car as an amplifier. Treat ang > 40 rad/s or vy > ~250 studs/s on two consecutive samples (reuse the wdSpeedStrikes pattern) as a "fling" verdict -> violate(), which already zeroes linear and angular velocity and revokes ownership. summary: Police cars run the shared VehicleController on the server, and it writes five replicated VectorForce.Force properties per car every PreSimulation. That floods every client with property-change traffic.
evidence: PoliceService.luau:2099-2110 calls unit.controller:step(d) every PreSimulation for each unit. The controller is created with isServer=true at :921. In VehicleController.luau the step writes `w.force.Force = up * (mass * a)` for each wheel at :617/:624, `self.drive.Force = ...` at :679/:688, and toggles upright.Enabled at :702-704. These are ordinary instance properties under Workspace, so every server write replicates. StreamingEnabled=false (default.project.json:36) means it goes to all clients. Suspension compression changes every frame, so the values are never identical. Estimate: 14 units x 5 properties x 60 Hz is about 4,200 property updates/s per client (about 34k/s server-wide for 8 clients). At about 20-25 bytes each that is roughly 80-100 KB/s per client before any engine coalescing, far above a comfortable mobile receive budget. Smaller server-side costs in the same path: serverNow() builds a pcall closure on every step (:321-326, called at :642); _pollAttributes calls _suppressForeignMovers, which does chassis:GetChildren() every 0.2 s per unit even though the server never has foreign movers (:488-516); and there are 4 raycasts per unit per frame (:612), about 3,360/s at 14 units.
failureScenario: With two or three 5-star players, 14 cruisers are active. Every phone receives thousands of VectorForce updates per second for cars it may not even see. Physics replication for the players' own and nearby cars is queued behind this traffic, so cars rubber-band and network ping rises. Low-end mobile clients spike on Network Receive and drop frames during every big chase.
suggestedFix: In VehicleController, when self.isServer is true, do not use VectorForce instances. Compute the same forces and apply them as impulses each step: `chassis:ApplyImpulseAtPosition(up * mass * a * dt, hub)` per wheel and `chassis:ApplyImpulse(driveForce * dt)`. Impulses are not replicated properties. Keep the Upright AlignOrientation but toggle it only on state change (already done). If VectorForce must stay, at least quantize writes (skip when the change is under about 2% of mass*g). Also in the server path: call Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() directly (no closure), skip _suppressForeignMovers, and cache the tires-popped state. Re-run tests/spec/police.spec.luau's kinematic chase sims to confirm stability, and verify the gain in the Developer Console Network tab (or Stats.DataReceiveKbps) during a 5-star chase.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Police is the only server-side user of VehicleController (PoliceService.luau:921, isServer=true), and it is stepped every PreSimulation (:2099-2110). step() writes w.force.Force for each wheel (VehicleController.luau:617/:624) and self.drive.Force (:679/:688). These are ordinary VectorForce properties in Workspace. Suspension and drive values change every frame, so every write replicates, and with StreamingEnabled=false (default.project.json:36) it goes to every client. The clients never use these values: police assemblies are server-owned (SetNetworkOwner(nil) at :919/:1825), and clients only receive their physics state. Estimate: 5 props x 60 Hz x 6 units is about 1.8k updates/s, roughly 35 KB/s, for one 5-star suspect. At 14 units it is about 4.2k updates/s, roughly 80 KB/s per client. Chases are the core loop, so this is frequent. Upright and MaxTorque are already written only on change. Two side claims are wrong. serverNow() runs only when _poppedUntil > 0, because the `and` short-circuits at :642, so it is not called every step. _suppressForeignMovers is a trivial GetChildren every 0.2 s. The 4 raycasts per unit per frame are inherent to a raycast car and cheap on the server.
fix: src/shared/Vehicle/VehicleController.luau: when self.isServer, do not create the Suspension_XX and Drive VectorForces. Keep the Upright AlignOrientation, which is already toggled only on change. In step(), compute the same vectors and apply them as impulses on the server-owned assembly. For each grounded wheel: `chassis:ApplyImpulseAtPosition(up * (mass * a * dt), hub)`. For the drive: `chassis:ApplyImpulse((fwd*aF + right*aLat - groundUp*aDown) * (mass*scale) * dt)`. Leave the client path unchanged. Make _zeroForces and destroy() tolerate missing movers. Update tests/spec/vehicle.spec.luau: 'new() creates the movers' should assert that VectorForces exist only for isServer=false, and 'foreign movers are suppressed' should build the foreign controller as a client one. tests/harness.luau:131-132 already stubs ApplyImpulse and ApplyImpulseAtPosition. Fallback if impulses change handling: keep the VectorForces but cache the last written value, and write only when |new-last| > 0.02*mass*g per wheel or 0.05*mass*g for the drive. Verify with Stats.DataReceiveKbps or the Developer Console Network tab during a 5-star chase.

summary: Each traffic car's AlignPosition.Position is rewritten every server Heartbeat, so every moving traffic car sends a replicated property update to every client each frame, on top of its normal physics replication.
evidence: TrafficService.luau:1243-1265 runs step(frameDt) every Heartbeat. step() at :1102-1112 recomputes the carrot and sets `ap.Position = target` and `ao.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.zero, heading)` for every entry. The movers are created at :838-860 and parented to the chassis in Workspace. The carrot advances every frame while the car moves, so Position changes every frame. AlignOrientation changes only during turn arcs; same-value writes on straight lanes should not replicate. Estimate: BASE_COUNT 18 rising to MAX_COUNT 36 (:47-48) at 60 Hz is about 1,100-2,200 Position updates/s per client, plus orientation updates in turns. With StreamingEnabled off, every client gets them for every car on the map. There is also a CFrame allocation per car per frame (:1111).
failureScenario: During Rush Hour (traffic x2), every client receives about 2k+ AlignPosition updates per second for cars all over the island. Combined with PERF-01, this saturates mobile receive bandwidth, and both traffic cars and the player's own car jitter.
suggestedFix: Drive traffic with movers whose targets rarely change. Use a LinearVelocity (VelocityConstraintMode.Vector, finite MaxForce) set to heading*v plus a small lane-correction term, and an AlignOrientation or AngularVelocity for yaw. On a straight lane at cruise these targets stay constant, so nothing replicates. Write them only when they change by more than an epsilon (for example 0.5 stud/s or 1 degree), and only from the turn arc or when braking. If you keep AlignPosition, throttle writes to about 10 Hz with a velocity-lead target and lower Responsiveness to avoid stop-go motion. Either way, track the last written value per entry and skip redundant writes.
verifyReason: Confirmed. step() runs every Heartbeat (TrafficService.luau:1243-1265) and, for every live entry, sets `ap.Position = target` and `ao.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(...)` (:1109-1112). The carrot advances every frame while the car moves, so AlignPosition.Position replicates every frame for every moving traffic car, to every client, on top of the cars' normal physics replication. AlignOrientation writes are identical on straight lanes, and identical writes do not replicate, so the extra cost there is only during turn arcs. This cost is always on whenever anyone is online: BASE_COUNT is 18, which is about 1.1k updates/s or roughly 20 KB/s per client, and it doubles to MAX_COUNT 36 during rush hour. That makes it as large as PERF-01 and more persistent.
fix: src/server/Systems/TrafficService.luau: stop writing a new target every frame. Preferred: replace the AlignPosition (spawnTraffic :838-860) with a LinearVelocity (VelocityConstraintMode.Vector, MaxForce = mass*g*10, RelativeTo World). Set VectorVelocity = heading*e.v plus a clamped correction toward the carrot, k*(target - pos) with Y included to hold ride height. Quantize it to 0.5 stud/s and write it only when it differs from a per-entry cached value. Write ao.CFrame only when heading changes by more than about 1 degree. On straight lanes at cruise, nothing then replicates. Alternative with less tuning: keep AlignPosition but write at most every 0.1 s. Use a lead target about 0.5 s ahead on the path and set ap.MaxVelocity to max(e.v, 1), rounded to 1 stud/s and written only on change, so the car runs at v instead of stop-start. Keep the KNOCKED_OFF_DIST check against the true carrot.

summary: Police helicopters are animated on the server every Heartbeat (anchored body CFrame, rotor Weld.C0, searchlight disc CFrame). This replicates three properties per heli per frame and looks choppy on clients because anchored-part moves are not interpolated.
evidence: PoliceService.luau:2139-2152 calls updateHeli every Heartbeat for each heli. updateHeli sets `body.CFrame` on the anchored root (:1706; the body is anchored at :1344 and every other part is welded to it), sets `rotorWeld.C0` to spin the rotor (:1708-1712), sets `disc.CFrame` on a second anchored part (:1714-1718), and blinks siren Transparency every 0.35 s (:1720-1730). With MAX_HELIS=3 (:115), that is up to 540 replicated property changes/s per client, and the rotor spin is purely cosmetic server work. The same pattern appears in EventService.luau:842-857 (dropIn calls PivotTo every Heartbeat for about 1 s per hot drop), though there it is one-off.
failureScenario: At 4+ stars, every client receives a constant stream of heli CFrame/C0 updates. Anchored CFrame updates arrive at network cadence without interpolation, so the chopper and its spinning rotor visibly stutter on phones under load, while still costing bandwidth on top of PERF-01 and PERF-02.
suggestedFix: Keep the heli's logical state on the server: heli.pos and yaw are already all that heliSight and updateHeliCeiling need. Replicate only that state, for example as model attributes (TargetPos, Yaw, Leaving) updated at 5-10 Hz or only when they change meaningfully. Do the rendering on clients: interpolate the body CFrame, spin the rotor via a local Weld.C0, place the disc, and blink the sirens (EffectsController already blinks police-car sirens locally). Alternatively make the body an unanchored, server-owned root moved by a LinearVelocity whose target changes at 10 Hz, so physics replication interpolates it. In both cases, stop writing rotorWeld.C0 and the siren transparency on the server.
verifyReason: Confirmed. updateHeli runs every server Heartbeat for each heli (PoliceService.luau:2139-2152). Each run writes body.CFrame on the anchored root (:1706), rotorWeld.C0 (:1708-1712) and the anchored SpotDisc CFrame (:1714-1718), and it toggles siren Transparency every 0.35 s. No client code touches helis (grep in src/client finds nothing), so all animation is server-replicated. Anchored CFrame and C0 changes arrive as property updates with no interpolation, so motion is choppy under network jitter. Cost per heli is 3 x 60 property updates/s, roughly 5 KB/s, with at most MAX_HELIS=3 (about 15 KB/s), and only at 4+ stars. That is smaller than PERF-01 and PERF-02 but visible. EventService.dropIn is a one-off of about 1 s and not worth changing.
fix: src/server/Systems/PoliceService.luau updateHeli: stop writing rotorWeld.C0 and the siren Transparency, and stop writing body and disc CFrames every frame. The server keeps heli.pos, vel and yaw as the logical state; heliSight and updateHeliCeiling already use only that. At about 10 Hz, publish a few attributes on the heli model: HeliPos (Vector3), HeliYaw/Pitch/Roll, SpotPos and Leaving. Add a small client renderer in src/client/Controllers/EffectsController.luau (tag the model, for example 'PoliceHeli', in spawnHeli). It should interpolate toward the attributes each RenderStepped, PivotTo the anchored body locally (the server no longer writes it, so there is no fight), place the disc, spin RotorWeld.C0 and blink the sirens. Cheaper interim step: move only the rotor spin and siren blink to the client, and throttle the body and disc writes to about 15 Hz.

summary: Traffic follows players by destroying cars that end up more than 650 studs from everyone and building brand-new ones 150-450 studs away, so fast drivers keep the spawner at its 2 cars/s cap. Each spawn is a full procedural CarBuilder build plus an NPC model replicated to every client.
evidence: Tuning: SPAWN_RING {150,450}, DESPAWN_DIST 650, SPAWNS_PER_TICK 2, MANAGE_TICK 1 (TrafficService.luau:57-61, :83). managePass destroys cars beyond DESPAWN_DIST (:1178-1186) and spawns up to 2 per tick (:1213-1215). spawnTraffic (:793-914) calls VehicleService.spawn, which runs CarBuilder.buildDef (VehicleService.luau:616): up to 40 parts plus WeldConstraints, wheel welds, attachments, headlight SpotLights, mutation GetDescendants and sort. It also runs buildDriver (8 parts + 7 welds, :550-622), adds AlignPosition/AlignOrientation and a Carjack prompt, and the managed prompts are refreshed. Estimate: a player driving at about 100 studs/s leaves a newly spawned car behind within about 5-10 s, so with 18-27 target cars the pass runs at its cap of about 2 builds and 2 destroys per second. Each is roughly 100-130 instances, so each client receives about 250 instance creations and deletions per second. Each new car also fires client tag and descendant handlers: WheelAnimator.track, SoundController.trackCar, EffectsController.trackVehicle, and DealershipClient's Vehicles.DescendantAdded→watchPrompt for every descendant (DealershipClient.luau:591).
failureScenario: Someone boosts down the ring road, and every second two cars are built and torn down near them. Mobile clients see recurring replication bursts and GC spikes (hitches every 0.5-1 s while driving), and the server spends steady CPU rebuilding identical procedural cars.
suggestedFix: Recycle cars instead of destroying them. In managePass, take a car that is beyond DESPAWN_DIST and relocate it: reset its path state with e.path = TrafficService._newPath(axis, line, dir, s, pick), call VehicleService.teleport(car, laneCF * CFrame.new(0, ride + 0.3, 0)), reset e.v, ap.Position and the blocked/ghost timers, and optionally re-roll the NPC colours. Only the CFrame then replicates. Destroy and build only when the target count changes. Also bias spawn and relocation points ahead of the anchor player's velocity (for example anchor + vel.Unit * 300) so fast drivers don't immediately strand new cars, and add hysteresis so cars ahead of a moving player are kept.
verifyReason: Confirmed mechanism. managePass (TrafficService.luau:1171-1218) destroys traffic cars more than 650 studs from all players and spawns up to SPAWNS_PER_TICK=2 per second. Each spawn is a full CarBuilder.buildDef (VehicleService.luau:616) plus the NPC, movers, Carjack prompt and Touched hook, and each one replicates to every client. Despawn uses the minimum distance over all players, so in a full 8-player server spread over the 1600-stud map most cars stay within 650 of someone and churn drops. The cost shows up when one or a few clustered players drive fast; car top speeds are 66-190 studs/s. Each churn event is about 100+ instances built, replicated and torn down, plus client tag handlers. This is real but conditional, so medium is right.
fix: src/server/Systems/TrafficService.luau managePass: recycle instead of destroy-and-spawn when the count is not shrinking. For an entry beyond DESPAWN_DIST, pick a new lane with the same ring search as trySpawnNear, then reset its state. Set e.path = TrafficService._newPath(axis, line, dir, s, pick). Call VehicleService.teleport(car, CFrame.lookAt(pos, pos+heading) * CFrame.new(0, ride + 0.3, 0)); this resets the watchdog. Zero the chassis linear and angular velocity, then set it to heading*e.v. Set e.v = e.cruise*0.6 and ap.Position to the new target. Reset blockedSince, blockerKind, ghostUntil, holdStopUntil and nearPed, and restore car.health and the Health attribute. Destroy and spawn only when target - count changes. Recycling keeps the old carId and mutation, so luck events (EventService getLuck) no longer affect recycled cars. Re-roll by rebuilding a small fraction of cars, or all of them when luck changes. Also bias trySpawnNear's ring toward the anchor's velocity (anchor + vel.Unit*~250 when speed > 40) so new cars aren't immediately stranded behind a fast driver.

summary: With StreamingEnabled=false, every mobile client holds every car model, plot display car and SurfaceGui on the map and receives all of their property churn (PERF-01/02/03/08). At the target scale that is roughly 17-18k parts plus a few hundred render-to-texture GUIs per phone.
evidence: default.project.json:36 has StreamingEnabled=false (a decision recorded in SPEC.md:44, 'revisit ... if mobile memory is an issue'). Car models at scale: up to 44 parked (StreetSpawnService.luau:36), 36 traffic each with an 8-part NPC (TrafficService.luau:48), 14 police (Config/Police.luau:12), about 10 dealership cars, and up to 96 garage display cars (12 pads x 8 plots, Economy.luau:14-15). The display cars are full CarBuilder models built on the server (GarageService.luau:479). At ≤40 parts per car (SPEC.md:248) that is about 200 cars and about 8,000 car parts on top of the ≤9,000-part map. PlotService adds about 35 SurfaceGuis per plot (PadGui and SignGui per pad at 24-30 PixelsPerStud, :287/:322, MaxDistance 400 at :170). Physics replication for about 50 moving server-owned assemblies also goes to everyone regardless of distance. CarBuilder already sets ModelStreamingMode=Atomic (CarBuilder.luau:1907), so cars are ready for streaming.
failureScenario: A full 8-player server on a 2-3 GB Android phone: client memory sits high from instances plus GUI textures, and every police, traffic or heli update anywhere on the 1,600-stud island is downloaded. Low-memory devices crash or are force-closed mid-session, which is the main audience for this genre.
suggestedFix: Turn StreamingEnabled on with StreamingTargetRadius of about 400-512 and StreamingMinRadius of about 192, keep cars Atomic, and mark key plot and POI models Persistent where client code needs them immediately. Most client code is already tag- or WaitForChild-based; audit any direct Workspace.X.Y chains before enabling it. Independently of streaming, stop server-building the 96 display cars: replicate only an anchored prompt anchor per pad plus attributes (CarId, Mutation, Income), and have GarageClient build the CarBuilder model locally only for plots within about 300 studs. That removes about 3,800 replicated parts.
verifyReason: The fact is correct: StreamingEnabled=false (default.project.json:36), so every client holds every car, plot and GUI and receives all property churn. But SPEC.md:44 records this as a deliberate v1 decision for 8-player servers. The 17-18k-part figure is a theoretical ceiling: 96 display cars requires all 8 players with all 12 pads filled, and not every car uses 40 parts. Part counts in the ~15k range are common on mobile without streaming. The concrete network waste is better fixed at the source (PERF-01, 02, 03), and the GUI memory belongs under PERF-12. Turning streaming on now is a broad behaviour change with correctness risk for client code that indexes Workspace directly, and nothing here has measured a memory problem.
fix: First fix PERF-01, 02 and 03, then measure client memory (Developer Console > Memory) and network receive on a low-end Android device in a full 8-player server. Change anything only if memory is high or devices crash. If they do: set Workspace StreamingEnabled=true in default.project.json with StreamingTargetRadius about 512 and StreamingMinRadius about 192. Cars already use ModelStreamingMode Atomic (CarBuilder.luau:1907). Set ModelStreamingMode=Persistent on the plot models (PlotService), the dealership and POI models that client code needs at join. Audit src/client for direct Workspace.X.Y chains and switch them to WaitForChild or tag-based lookup. Update SPEC.md:44. Client-built display cars are a much larger refactor; do it only if measurement shows display cars dominate.

summary: AssetLibrary loads about 110 runtime models (35 hero car shells, props, buildings) and publishes the templates into ReplicatedStorage, but nothing in the shipped code consumes them. Every client downloads and holds them for nothing.
evidence: AssetLibrary.luau:226-233 creates ReplicatedStorage.AssetLibrary, and :212 parents each normalized template under it (Assets.luau has about 110 entries; Hero shells are about 9K tris with 2K textures according to ART_PASS.md:7). The only references to AssetLibrary in src/ are Config/Assets.luau, AssetLibrary.luau and init.server.luau. CarBuilder never reads Hero templates, and the MapDresser system described in ART_PASS.md:22-28 does not exist in src/server/Systems. MapBuilder only tags AssetSlot placeholders (MapBuilder.luau:488). Templates in ReplicatedStorage replicate their full instance data, including MeshPart physics data, to every client at join. Mesh and texture content may load lazily, so the exact memory cost depends on the assets. Check with Developer Console > Memory (Instances/PlaceMemory).
failureScenario: Each mobile join downloads about 110 unused models. Once the planned hero shells are wired into CarBuilder, about 200 cars x 9K tris is about 1.8M triangles, plus up to 35 distinct 2K texture sets, which would exceed mobile GPU budgets.
suggestedFix: Until a consumer exists, keep templates in ServerStorage (not replicated), or skip loading them. When CarBuilder and MapDresser consume them, clone on the server only what gets placed. Set MeshPart.RenderFidelity to Automatic, CollisionFidelity to Box (CanCollide is false anyway), and DoubleSided false. Cap textures at 1K for vehicles and share atlases. Combined with streaming (PERF-05), use hero shells only for driven or nearby cars and procedural bodies elsewhere.
verifyReason: Confirmed: AssetLibrary publishes about 108 loaded templates to ReplicatedStorage.AssetLibrary (AssetLibrary.luau:212, :226-233), and nothing in src consumes them. There are no HeroMesh or AssetLibrary references outside Config/Assets, AssetLibrary and init.server, and there is no MapDresser system. Every client therefore receives the template instances, including MeshPart data, at join for no benefit. The impact is low today: mesh and texture content loads lazily, the cost is mostly one-time at join, and the art pass that will consume these (task #4) is still pending. The suggested runtime setting of RenderFidelity, CollisionFidelity and DoubleSided would not work, because scripts cannot write those properties at runtime.
fix: src/server/Systems/AssetLibrary.luau init(): parent the root folder to ServerStorage instead of ReplicatedStorage until a consumer exists. Alternatively, put a Config/Assets flag on AssetLibrary.start() and skip loading entirely. When CarBuilder or MapDresser starts consuming templates, the server should clone only what it places into Workspace. Set mesh fidelity at import or upload time, or load through AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(meshId, { CollisionFidelity = Box, RenderFidelity = Automatic }). Cap vehicle textures at about 1K when uploading, and update the path comments in Config/Assets.luau and docs/ART_PASS.md.

summary: On every client, WheelAnimator updates the 25 nearest cars every PreRender, with up to 4 suspension raycasts and 4 Weld.C0 writes per car and no frustum or device-tier culling. On a flat road grid this is mostly wasted work on phones.
evidence: Budgets are RANGE 250, HOT_COUNT 25, COLD_PER_FRAME 6 and BOB_RANGE 140 (WheelAnimator.luau:26-28, :34). onPreRender (:390-442) calls updateRig for up to 25 hot cars plus 6 cold cars each frame. animateWheels casts one ray per wheel for non-driven cars within 140 studs (:349-355) and writes `w.weld.C0 = WheelAnimator.wheelC0(...)` for all 4 wheels (:364), building 5 CFrames per wheel. The rays exclude Vehicles (refreshFilter, :204-226), so they only hit the map, and the roads are flat (ROAD_Y=0); traffic floats at a fixed height on AlignPosition. Estimate at a busy intersection: 10-15 moving cars within 140 studs means 40-60 raycasts and 60-100 C0 writes per frame (about 2.4k-3.6k raycasts/s), even for cars behind the camera. CarBuilder uses plain Welds for wheels (CarBuilder.luau:507-513), so the animation goes through C0 joint updates rather than Motor6D.Transform.
failureScenario: A mobile player in downtown traffic with a police chase nearby loses 1-3 ms per frame to cosmetic wheel bob and spin, enough to drop a mid-range phone below 30 fps while driving.
suggestedFix: Tier the budget by device, for example HOT_COUNT 8 and RANGE 150 when TouchEnabled and not KeyboardEnabled, or adapt to measured frame time. Skip cars that are off-screen (cheap WorldToViewportPoint or a camera dot-product check). Drop bob raycasts for non-driven cars: use offset 0, or a small velocity-based fake bob, and keep rays only for the 2-3 nearest cars or stunt-park zones. Write C0 only when spin or steer changed by more than about 2 degrees. Longer term, switch CarBuilder wheel joints to Motor6D and animate .Transform.
verifyReason: Confirmed as code: up to HOT_COUNT=25 plus COLD_PER_FRAME=6 cars per PreRender, a raycast per wheel for non-driven cars within BOB_RANGE=140 (WheelAnimator.luau:349-355), 4 Weld.C0 writes per car (:364), and no frustum or device tiering. The claimed cost is overstated, for three reasons. Settled parked and anchored cars return early (:313-331), and display and dealer cars only get the rainbow effect, so only moving cars cost anything. Realistically about 10-15 moving cars are near the camera. Short client raycasts take microseconds. Expect well under 1 ms per frame on mid-range phones, not 1-3 ms. The bob rays against flat roads are mostly wasted, as stated.
fix: src/client/Controllers/WheelAnimator.luau: (1) Tier by device. If UserInputService.TouchEnabled and not KeyboardEnabled, use HOT_COUNT about 10, RANGE about 160 and BOB_RANGE about 40. (2) In onPreRender, skip non-driven rigs behind the camera: (pos - camPos):Dot(cam.CFrame.LookVector) < -10. (3) Skip bob raycasts for traffic cars, which hold a fixed height via AlignPosition (model Kind == 'Traffic'). (4) Skip the C0 write when the spin, steer and offset deltas since the last write are tiny. Switching to Motor6D.Transform is optional and longer-term.

summary: The 1 Hz income tick writes a replicated 'Uncollected' attribute on every garage display car and plot every second, and forces a full DataSnapshot rebuild and push to each player every 3 s. That is constant attribute churn plus UI refresh work on every client.
evidence: GarageService.luau:1392-1407 ticks every Economy.INCOME_TICK=1 s. tickPlayer sets d.model:SetAttribute('Uncollected', whole) on every display car whose whole-dollar value changed (:1250-1255, so effectively every car every second), and sets the plot 'Uncollected' attribute (:629-631). Every SNAPSHOT_EVERY=3 ticks (:33) it calls markDirty (:1264-1267), which queues DataService.buildSnapshot (DataService.luau:800-818, :944-1030). The snapshot calls hasPass for every pass, slotSnapshots, multiplier, incomePerSec and 3 Rewards views, then FireClients the whole profile view including discovered, stats and contracts. Clients: GarageClient's refreshUncollected runs Format.cash and rewrites a TextScaled label on every display car each second, even for other players' cars where the label is hidden (:281-290). Each snapshot triggers HUD refreshIncome and refreshBadges, and MenuController queueRefresh (:3437); with the Index open, refreshIndex spawns a new Kit.tweenNumber per-frame thread (:1978). Estimate: up to 96 display-car attribute updates/s to each of 8 clients (about 3-4 KB/s each), plus about 1-3 KB per player every 3 s for snapshots. Autosave writes without relying on this push (DataService.luau:1194-1207).
failureScenario: In a full server, every phone re-lays out about 96 TextScaled labels per second for garages it isn't looking at, and every 3 s each player's open menu rebuilds itself, so scroll positions jitter and number tweens restart even though nothing the player did changed.
suggestedFix: Replicate accrual parameters instead of the ticking value: set 'Income' and 'UncollectedBase' plus 'AccrualAt' (server time) only on park, collect or multiplier change, and let GarageClient compute the live amount at about 4 Hz only for the owner's own plot (others never see the label). Remove the every-3-ticks markDirty. If the dirty flag still matters, add a DataService.markDirtySilent that sets profile.dirty and changeGen without queuePush. Push snapshots only on discrete state changes (collect, purchase, unlock, contract progress).

summary: The traffic spacing scan is an all-pairs O(T x (cars + players)) loop at 10 Hz, and it allocates a fresh copy of every vehicle on each pass.
evidence: scanPass (TrafficService.luau:964-1066) runs every SCAN_TICK=0.1 s (:82). It calls VehicleService.all(), which builds a new array of every registered car, parked and dealership included (VehicleService.luau:566-572), then for each traffic entry loops over every obstacle (:984-1034). _aheadDistance recomputes fwd:Cross per pair (:484-496). Inside the loop, a static-blocked car calls minDist(pos, playerRoots()), which allocates another table (:1052). Estimate: 36 traffic x about 70 obstacles is about 2.5k cone tests per scan, about 25k/s, plus a roughly 110-element array allocated 10 times a second. That is a few ms of server CPU per second: noticeable but not critical.
failureScenario: In Rush Hour with 8 players the scan becomes the largest Lua cost in TrafficService and adds GC pressure on the server, eating headroom needed by police AI and physics.
suggestedFix: Bucket obstacles into a coarse grid (for example 40-stud cells, or by road line and axis, since traffic only cares about its own lane) and test only the current and next cells. Reject by squared distance against SLOW_DIST before any dot or cross product. Precompute each car's right vector once per scan. Reuse a module-level scratch array instead of VehicleService.all(), or expose a non-allocating iterator, and compute playerRoots once per scan.

summary: Police spawn and rubber-band lane search calls VehicleService.all(), which allocates a full vehicle list, once per candidate lane, and raycasts per candidate.

Each passing candidate calls isClearOfVehicles (:789-808), which loops over units and then calls VehicleService.all() (a fresh array of about 110 cars, :797) and iterates it. summary: The server writes Lighting.ClockTime at 10 Hz and about 9 lighting and post-effect properties at 2 Hz. Each write replicates and makes every client re-evaluate sun and lighting.
evidence: LightingService.luau:421-437 sets Lighting.ClockTime every CLOCK_INTERVAL=0.1 s (:30) and applyLook every ENV_INTERVAL=0.5 s (:31). applyLook (:234-250) writes Ambient, OutdoorAmbient, Brightness, ExposureCompensation, TintColor, Atmosphere Color/Decay and Bloom Intensity. The sun moves about 0.0017 h per write, below visible resolution, but each change invalidates sun direction and shadows on every client (Future lighting is set at :350 and in default.project.json).
failureScenario: On low-end mobile, the constant tiny sun-direction changes add steady background lighting work, and every client receives about 30 lighting property updates per second.
suggestedFix: Replicate the cycle epoch once (a Lighting attribute such as CycleStart in server time) and compute ClockTime and applyLook on each client locally at 1-2 Hz. Or keep it server-side but quantize ClockTime to about 0.05 h steps and update it at 1 Hz.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Lighting.ClockTime is written every 0.1 s (LightingService.luau:30, :421-426), and applyLook writes 8-9 lighting and post-effect properties every 0.5 s (:234-250). The server keeps isNight and setNight for the street lights.

summary: Managed Enter/Hotwire prompts are destroyed and recreated on every enter/exit and added to the car's trove each time, but never removed from it. The trove holds a growing list of destroyed prompt instances for the car's lifetime.
evidence: refreshManagedPrompts (VehicleService.luau:1224-1277) runs on every setDriver (:854) and seat() (:943, :954, :972). It creates a new EnterPrompt via createEnterPrompt, which does st.trove:Add(pp) (:1220), or a new Hotwire prompt via addStealPrompt, which does st.trove:Add(prompt) (:1121). When the state flips back it calls :Destroy() on the old prompt (:1251-1254, :1273-1276) but leaves the entry in trove._items (Trove.luau:19-22). Everything else in this lens checked out as clean: VehicleService.destroy cleans state, trove and byModel (:1360-1389); TrafficService.release cleans movers, prompt and Touched (:686-712); PoliceService.removeUnit destroys the trove and controller (:711-731); client troves (VehicleClient session, GarageClient displays, CombatClient characters) are cleaned. Network ownership is set once on spawn (:683) and re-asserted only on change (PoliceService.luau:1823-1826). No client fires remotes per frame.
failureScenario: An Owned car that a player hops in and out of 100 times before it is towed home keeps 100+ destroyed ProximityPrompt references (and their Lua wrappers) alive until the car is destroyed. The leak is small but unbounded per car lifetime.
suggestedFix: Don't put managed prompts in st.trove. Track them only in st.enterPrompt and st.hotwirePrompt and destroy those two explicitly in VehicleService.destroy, which already nils them at :1382-1383. Alternatively, toggle prompt.Enabled instead of destroying and recreating, which also removes the per-toggle Instance.new and replication.
verifyReason: Confirmed. createEnterPrompt does st.trove:Add(pp) (VehicleService.luau:1220), and addStealPrompt does st.trove:Add(prompt) (:1121). refreshManagedPrompts (:1224-1277) destroys and recreates these prompts on every state flip without removing the old ones from trove._items (Trove.luau:19-22). Each enter and exit cycle therefore leaves a destroyed-Instance reference in the trove for the car's lifetime. The leak is tiny and bounded by car lifetime. The destroy and recreate also replicates new instances on every toggle.
fix: src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau: stop adding managed prompts to st.trove. In createEnterPrompt, remove `st.trove:Add(pp)`. In addStealPrompt, add an opts flag (for example `managed = true`) that skips the trove add at :1121, and pass it from refreshManagedPrompts. Other callers, such as TrafficService's Carjack prompt, keep the current behaviour. No other cleanup is needed: prompts are parented to the chassis, and VehicleService.destroy already calls model:Destroy() after nil-ing st.enterPrompt and st.hotwirePrompt (:1382-1387).
